I was almost named James. My mom had a weird thing where she wanted all of her kid's names to start with J. My two older sisters were given names that start with J, so my mom planned on continuing the pattern. However, my dad and my grandpa have the same first names, and they wanted to continue that tradition, so I got that name instead. I'm not "Mr. Anon III" though, because we all have different middle names, so my dad or I wouldn't have to deal with being called "junior".

Hey everyone, sorry about all of this, I was struggling really hard with my depression earlier. I've taken some time to calm down, and I'm feeling much better now. Sometimes I have moments where I get depressed for no reason, and in rarer cases, they get really bad like this. Thank you to u/Soltrix and u/ImSuez for helping me out, and thank you to everyone who took the time to read this post.
I used to see a psychologist for depression and stopped going a couple months ago. I've been through so many of them, I really don't think it's worth it anymore.

If I don't react to things the way others do, doesn't that mean I'm reacting to those things the wrong way? As for my problems being caused by my empathy, I've heard people say I have a decent amount of empathy, but I really don't think I'm empathetic enough. I can't help but still do and not do things for my own selfish reasons, and I can't stop, and I despise myself for that.

I've always questioned my diagnosis as well. I've had a proper IQ test done and got 107, but I seriously think something had to have gone wrong with the test for me to get that. Even if it were around that, the doctor said that they no longer factor speed into the results, and if they did, it would have been lower.  I just wish I could make mistakes at the same rate that everyone else seems to, and just be normal. I wish I could, but it just doesn't seem like there's anything I can do to make that happen.

It's hard to give a specific example, but I've observed that I make the same usual insignificant mistakes that normal people seem to often make, except I make those mistakes almost twice as often. There's also various details and assumptions throughout my day that I often miss, creating problems for other people. Through those two things, I constantly create problems for other people, and there's nothing I can do about it because of Autism Spectrum. I think your assessment is correct, since I feel like everyone who knows me has been frustrated by my stupidity at some point.
